wikiGoal:
# Benchmark documentation brief

Create a source-grounded wiki for engineers who must understand, operate, debug, and safely change this repository.

- Explain the architecture, ownership boundaries, core data/control flows, persistence, external integrations, configuration, and failure handling.
- Include a practical quickstart and focused change guides for representative maintenance tasks.
- Treat source code and tests as authoritative. Cite concrete source evidence for every non-obvious technical claim.
- State uncertainty when the repository does not establish a fact. Do not invent runtime behavior, guarantees, or deployment details.
- Prefer a coherent, non-overlapping taxonomy over exhaustive file-by-file narration.

pages.title: Skills, Plugins, and Worker Isolation
pages.purpose: Cover the extension surface around the agent runtime: skills search/install service, plugins management, the isolated plugin worker process and protocol, extension preflight/diagnostics, and bundled skills CLI/search helpers.
instructions: Distinguish Pi package-manager-driven extension loading from desktop-managed skills/plugins UI flows.
Note terminal-only extension incompatibility handling if the code establishes it.

pages.title: Agent Host: Sessions, Models, and Runtime
pages.purpose: Document the Agent Host core: RPC handler registration, live session lifecycle in rpc-manager, persistence and watching of ~/.pi/agent sessions, model catalog and provider auth flows, and per-session tool environment.
instructions: Cover session index/monitoring and offline model catalog behavior as implemented.
Explain how sessions are shared with the pi CLI and what happens on host crash/restart regarding in-flight sessions.

pages.title: IPC Contract and Host Supervision
pages.purpose: Document the typed MessagePort RPC layer: wire protocol, Api/Streams contract, desktop preload bridge, renderer connection lifecycle, main-process system IPC, and the reverse host-rpc channel.
instructions: Cite the RPC wire protocol types and HostManager supervision constants with line ranges.
Trace at least one full request path (e.g. sessions.list) from renderer call to host handler and back, and one streaming path.

pages.title: Process Model and Ownership Boundaries
pages.purpose: Explain the Electron three-process model (Main, Agent Host utilityProcess, Renderer), ownership boundaries, message/data flow between them, and the top-level source directory taxonomy.
instructions: Cover what Main must NOT do (no business logic per main.ts header) and the no-TCP-server invariant.
Describe responsibilities and ownership boundaries per the code, not the README marketing text.

pages.title: Security and Isolation Model
pages.purpose: Aggregate the security model: renderer sandbox and CSP, preload location/message trust policies, IPC trust validation, file-access allowed roots, credential vault storage, redaction of secrets, and the separation of Browser vs managed-process vs coding permissions.
instructions: Enumerate fail-closed behaviors and where redaction is applied.
Include what the automated check scripts assert as security invariants.

pages.title: Built-in Browser Subsystem
pages.purpose: Document the Main-owned built-in browser: WebContentsView tab management, profiles and identity, network policy and sensitive-control handling, downloads, header rules, secret vault, authorization coordinator, persistent grants, and the capability-snapshot bridge to agent browser tools.
instructions: Explain the per-request validation chain (session, persistent policy, temporary grant, lease, policy revision) as implemented in source.
State the private-network best-effort caveat only if the code marks it.

pages.title: Build, Packaging, and Release Pipeline
pages.purpose: Explain the build and release pipeline: dev orchestration, tsup/vite build graph, electron-builder packaging configuration, bundled toolchains preparation, Windows helper/SBOM production steps, macOS signing/notarization scripts, and the GitHub Actions matrices.
instructions: Document what each gate enforces and where artifacts land.
Include the Rust helper and SBOM steps only for the packaging flows that run them.

pages.title: Message Channels (Telegram, Feishu/Lark, Weixin)
pages.purpose: Document IM message channels: the channel manager runtime, adapter registry, per-platform adapters (Telegram, Feishu/Lark, Weixin), pairing and session binding, lane scheduling, media handling, inbound policy, redaction, config/state stores, and secret access via Main.
instructions: Document that secrets live in the Main credential vault, not channel config files, if code confirms.
Explain how channel turns are serialized and how remote tool permission defaults are applied per session.

pages.title: Change Guide: Adding a Channel Adapter
pages.purpose: Change guide: adding or modifying a channel adapter — interface surface, registry wiring, secret handling, media and rendering responsibilities, and required focused tests.
instructions: Enumerate the registration, config, secret, and policy touchpoints a new or modified adapter needs.
Point at the closest existing adapter's test files as the template.

pages.title: Change Guide: Managed-Process Boundaries and Policy
pages.purpose: Change guide: safely changing managed-process capability gates, resource policy limits, backends, or cleanup deadlines without breaking the fail-closed guarantees and shutdown contracts.
instructions: Explain which layer (policy, capability, reaper, backend, UI) owns each kind of change and the invariants that must not regress.
Name the flood and workflow harnesses as verification.

pages.title: Change Guide: Extending the RPC Contract
pages.purpose: Change guide: adding or evolving an Api method or Stream topic across contract, host handlers, main request routing, and renderer usage, and keeping the contract coverage check satisfied.
instructions: Name every file that must change together and the command that proves coverage stays green.
Reference an existing method end-to-end as the worked example.

pages.title: Managed Development Processes
pages.purpose: Explain managed background development processes: capability gating, the Host-side service and worker, POSIX and Windows backends, output buffering and log cursors, agent tool contracts, LAN-bind confirmation, redaction, crash reaper journal, and bounded shutdown cleanup.
instructions: Document crash-recovery ownership via the reaper journal and owner identity.
Make the fail-closed gates explicit and the fact that this is lifecycle control, not a sandbox.

pages.title: Windows Managed Process Helper (Rust)
pages.purpose: Cover the native Windows x64 Rust helper: its protocol with the Host client, Job Object containment, build pipeline, integrity verification, and reproducibility/SBOM gates.
instructions: Document the protocol framing, state model, and integrity checks enforced by JS-side resolvers.
Include how packaging gates the helper's presence.

pages.title: Desktop Lifecycle and Operations
pages.purpose: Cover desktop lifecycle and operations: window creation/state, tray and badges, menus and command policy, deep links, single-instance handling, the update manager lifecycle, diagnostics export, crash reporter, and main logging.
instructions: Document quit-time ordering (managed process cleanup deadline, browser dispose) and what dialogs guard it.
State update platform support as the code gates it.

pages.title: Renderer Application Architecture
pages.purpose: Document the React renderer: app shell composition, the useAgentSession event pipeline, session/history state management, draft and layout persistence, i18n dictionaries, theming, and the API/event-stream clients.
instructions: Focus on how UI state is derived from host events and what is persisted where (localStorage vs disk).
Mention performance-critical paths (virtualized lists, caching) only if tests/code establish them.

pages.title: Testing and Quality Gates
pages.purpose: Document how code is verified here: the node:test convention and runner, contract coverage and dependency contract checks, Electron smoke and Browser E2E harnesses, managed-process flood/workflow harnesses, and the verify gate composition.
instructions: Document how the contract coverage tool links contract methods to handlers.
Give the exact command to run a single test file and explain fixture patterns shared across .test.mjs suites.

pages.title: Development Toolchain Management
pages.purpose: Document cross-platform development toolchain management: discovery and probing of system tools, the runtime/core catalog files, confirmed installs into app-private directories, download/extract integrity, environment construction and shims, and the revisioned snapshot sync consumed by the Agent Host runtime.
instructions: Document offline bundled rg/fd guarantees if the catalog and packaging establish them.
Explain the confirmation-gated install flow and what remains untouched on the host system.

pages.title: Quickstart and Task Routing
pages.purpose: Practical orientation: environment requirements, local development loop, day-to-day commands, and a task-routing map to the rest of the wiki for representative maintenance work.
instructions: List only commands that exist in package.json scripts.
Route concrete maintenance tasks (add an RPC method, add a channel adapter, change managed-process policy, build a package, debug a host crash) to the specific wiki page and script that owns them.
